newsitem.title: USA: US tax panel defeats ethanol tax subsidy plan.
newsitem.headline: US tax panel defeats ethanol tax subsidy plan.

text.p: The House Ways and Means Committee on Thursday defeated an amendment that would have retained tax subsidies for ethanol production by cutting back on corporate capital gains tax relief.
The measure, offered by Representatives Jim Nussle, a Republican from Iowa, and John Tanner, a Democrat from Tennessee, lost 21-17.
It aimed to overturn a provision of Committee Chairman Bill Archer's tax plan that would phase out the subsidies by 2000.
"There is only one ultimate answer and that is the free market economy," Archer said of the ethanol subsidies. "This distorts that," he said of the amendment.
He asserted that companies have sold farmers "a bill of goods" that ethanol production is the only way to make a profit.
"It is leading farmers into a dead alley," Archer said. "The highest and best use of corn is to feed human beings."
The Nussle and Tanner amendment would have retained ethanol subsidies by cutting back on corporate capital gains relief proposed by Archer.

Under the amendment, the capital gains rate would have been 34 percent in 1998, rather than Archer's proposed 32 percent, 33 percent for 1999, rather than 31 percent and 32.5 percent thereafter, rather than 30 percent.
Lawmakers were expected to vote later Thursday on other amendments on Archer's plan to phase out ethanol production subsidies.
Separately, the panel approved a measure that would clear farmers from the alternative minimum tax for sales of farm property and other installment sales.
This measure would be funded by restoring Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund Taxes.
Kenneth Kies, chief of staff for the Joint Committee on Taxation, said the storage tank taxes would only need to be extended for five years to cover the tax relief for farmers.
There were no other proposed amendments to the tax plan regarding the corporate and individual alternative minimum tax provisions.
